output.summary: Run is VALID with COMPLETE coverage. Capacity summary is BOUNDED with deterministic policy_verdict NO_VERDICT: lower_inclusive 197 users (highest verified PASS load) and upper_exclusive 297 users (achieved load of the failing step); capacity_knee is null because knee_reason is KNEE_DETECTOR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED. Step-1 (target 100) and step-2 (target 200) PASS with window p95 response time 140 ms vs 250 ms threshold; step-3 (target 300, achieved p05_10s 297) FAILs with observed p95 420 ms and window verdict FAIL (business_verdict FAIL). error_count is 0 across the run, so the failure is latency-only. Generator CPU summaries are identical across all three stages (mean 0.43, max 0.45, unit ratio) and the generator-cpu-guard (threshold 0.85) PASSes in every window; resource_verdict is NO_POLICY in every window. resource-binding reports clock_alignment not_verified_by_core, so temporal ordering between load and latency is not supported. Advice does not change the deterministic verdict.

hypotheses.observation: Stage-3 policy check FAILs: response_time_p95_ms observed 420 vs threshold 250 (lte); window-policy-summary stage-3 verdict FAIL (business_verdict FAIL), while stage-1 and stage-2 PASS with observed p95 140 ms. Capacity summary reports lower_inclusive 197 and upper_exclusive 297 for load_axis users.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The p95 jumped from 140 ms to 420 ms as achieved load rose from 197 to 297 users, with 0 errors across the run; this latency-only degradation is consistent with the service under test entering a queueing/saturation region near 300 users. However, the run contains only load-generator metrics, so the server-side cause is not evidenced by this analysis.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Repeat a sustained ~300-user stage while capturing service-under-test CPU, memory, GC, thread/connection-pool depth, and database metrics; compare per-10s-bin p95 with the 140 ms baseline seen at 100 and 200 users.

hypotheses.observation: Overall metric summary spans the full run: sample_count 3601, error_count 0, latency p50 136 ms, p95 417 ms, p99 420 ms, max 1500 ms, throughput_rps numerator 3601000 / denominator 900500; the checkout transaction summary reports the same values.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: Because the overall summary mixes all three windows, its p95/p99/max are dominated by the failing stage-3 window (p95 420 ms); the absence of errors means the observed degradation is a latency/queueing effect rather than request failures.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Plot per-window and per-10s-bin latency percentiles to confirm the p95 crossing is confined to stage-3 and to see whether the 1500 ms max occurs as an isolated spike or a sustained tail.

hypotheses.observation: Generator CPU summaries are numerically identical across all three stages: mean 0.43, min 0.41, max 0.45, sample_standard_deviation 0.01438 (unit ratio), while active_users rose from ~97-100 (stage-1) to ~297-300 (stage-3); generator-cpu-guard (operator gt, threshold 0.85) PASSes in all three windows.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The flat CPU series across tripled load could indicate the load generator is far from saturation, but could also be an instrumentation/sampling artifact (e.g., coarse aggregation or a constant reported value); the guard only confirms the series stayed below the 0.85 threshold, so it does not by itself establish generator headroom.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Inspect the raw per-cell generator CPU series and sampling resolution for stages 1-3; independently measure load-generator host utilization during a repeat run to confirm the metric responds to load.

hypotheses.observation: resource-binding reports mode explicit_windows, zero dropped cells, run/snapshot spans epoch ms 1767225600000-1767226500000, and clock_alignment 'not_verified_by_core'.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: With clock alignment unverified, the relative timing between load-generator activity and any external telemetry cannot be trusted, so a lead/lag ordering (e.g., latency rising only after load passes some level) cannot be supported as causal from this data alone.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Verify clock synchronization (e.g., NTP offset) on the load generator, service under test, and monitoring host before correlating load and latency timelines.

hypotheses.observation: Every window-policy-summary has resource_verdict NO_POLICY; capacity-summary reports bound_type BOUNDED, capacity_knee null, knee_reason KNEE_DETECTOR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED; facts are run_validity VALID, analysis_coverage COMPLETE, policy_verdict NO_VERDICT.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The analysis deliberately stops short of a capacity estimate: the highest verified PASS load is 197 users, the violation occurs at achieved 297 users, and without a resource policy or knee detector the verdict stays NO_VERDICT; NO_POLICY must not be read as a pass on server resources.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Add an explicit server-resource policy and run intermediate stages between 197 and 297 users (e.g., 220, 250, 275) to find where window p95 crosses 250 ms; enable/implement the knee detector to convert the bounds into a capacity estimate.

recommendations.action: Collect service-under-test resource and queue telemetry (CPU, memory, GC, thread/connection-pool depth, database) for a repeated ~300-user stage and compare it with the 100- and 200-user stages.
recommendations.rationale: Stage-3 is the only failing window (p95 420 ms > 250 ms) with zero errors; the run provides only load-generator metrics, so whether the latency increase comes from server saturation, configuration, or external factors cannot be confirmed from this analysis.

recommendations.action: Re-run with intermediate load levels between 197 and 297 users (for example 220, 250, 275) and record per-window p95.
recommendations.rationale: Capacity is bounded below by 197 (PASS) and above by 297 (achieved load at FAIL), with capacity_knee null, so the exact crossing where p95 exceeds 250 ms is unknown.

recommendations.action: Verify load-generator CPU metric fidelity and host capacity; inspect the raw generator CPU series and confirm it responds to load.
recommendations.rationale: Generator CPU summaries are identical across all three stages while user load triples; the guard PASS only shows the series stayed below the 0.85 threshold, not that the metric is trustworthy or that generator headroom is proven.

recommendations.action: Verify clock alignment (NTP/offset checks) across the load generator, service under test, and monitoring before any temporal correlation.
recommendations.rationale: resource-binding reports clock_alignment not_verified_by_core, so lead/lag or causal interpretations of load-vs-latency timing are unsupported.

recommendations.action: Add an explicit resource policy for the service under test and define the latency SLO at finer granularity; re-run to obtain a definitive verdict.
recommendations.rationale: resource_verdict is NO_POLICY in every window and overall policy_verdict is NO_VERDICT; missing policy is not a pass, and the current data cannot distinguish server-headroom from server-saturation behavior below the observed failure.

caveats: capacity_knee is null and knee_reason is KNEE_DETECTOR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED; upper_exclusive 297 is an exclusive bound, so the exact saturation point between 197 and 297 users is unknown.
The deterministic verdict NO_VERDICT is preserved; this advice does not change it.
resource_verdict NO_POLICY for all windows means no server-resource policy was evaluated; PASS windows do not demonstrate server health or headroom.
Only load-generator metrics (active_users, generator CPU) are present; no service-under-test resource data exists in this run, so the latency increase cannot be attributed to server saturation.
clock_alignment is not_verified_by_core; no temporal/causal ordering between load and latency is supported.
error_count 0 and error rate 0/3601 do not prove spare capacity or the absence of a problem; the failure is latency-only.
The overall metric summary (sample_count 3601) mixes all three stages; its p95 417 ms largely reflects stage-3 and must not be read as homogeneous run-wide behavior.
Generator CPU summaries are identical across stages, which may indicate coarse/aggregated instrumentation rather than genuinely constant utilization.
